title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 05/27 — "The Heat-Ray"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 5. A kind of fascination holds the narrator where he stands, knee-deep in the heather, staring at the mound of sand that hides them. He dares not go back and he cannot go home, so he walks a wide curve round the pit, hunting a point of vantage. A leash of black whips flashes across the sunset and is snatched back. A thin rod comes up out of the sand, joint by joint, and turns a mirror on the common.

The sunset fades. The crowd towards Woking grows and begins to murmur, the quiet gives people courage, and they come on in twos and threes until the ring is almost closed. Then men come out of Horsell with a white flag — a tablecloth on a pole, our whole argument that we could be talked to — and the pit answers with a flash, three puffs of green smoke, and a humped black shape lifting over the rim. An invisible finger of heat is drawn through the heather, and it passes him by.

Chapter V of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
